Vietnamese Electrical Equipment Firms Hit as Sanctions Disrupt Operations

HANOI, June 13 — The Vietnamese electrical equipment industry is facing mounting disruption after a series of sanctions targeting key companies came into effect this week, halting exports and freezing assets at several manufacturing sites. The measures, imposed by a coalition of Western nations citing security concerns, have led to immediate operational slowdowns across the sector.

Thu Duc Electro Mechanical JSC, a major player in transformer and switchgear production, confirmed Thursday that its overseas transactions have been suspended and shipments blocked at Ho Chi Minh City port. “We are working around the clock to assess the impact and maintain commitments to our clients, but the situation remains highly uncertain,” said Nguyen Van Linh, a spokesperson for the company.

Industry sources report at least five major factories operated by affected firms, including PowerGrid Innovate Ltd. and Mekong CircuitTech, have scaled back assembly lines due to shortages of imported components and inability to access foreign payment systems. The Vietnam Electrical Equipment Association said Thursday that the sanctions have placed “thousands of skilled jobs at risk” and could lead to delivery delays for critical infrastructure projects.

“These restrictions are having an immediate chilling effect on our manufacturing capacity and export revenues,” said association chairwoman Le Thi Hoa. “We urge all parties to engage in dialogue to find a constructive resolution.”

Analysts warn that prolonged disruption could weaken Vietnam’s role in global supply chains for electrical components. As of Thursday afternoon, no timeline had been given for either the lifting or intensification of the sanctions, leaving the industry’s outlook deeply uncertain.
